emily: Heads-up — hit a confusing 413 from the embeds endpoint in client integration tests. Request size looks fine but we were sending mixed dims (1024 + 512) in the same batch. Console shows only `413` with no hint.

ravi: Can you paste the request payload shape + headers? We should be returning a structured error like `400: mixed-dim-batch` or `413: payload-bytes` depending on cause. Right now clients can't auto-fix.

emily: Paste: ```POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-Id: web-sdk-2
Body: {"inputs": [[... 1024-floats ...], [... 512-floats ...]]}
``` Console error: `Request failed: 413` only. No route or quota -> we retried and got same.

tim: If it's mixed dims we should be fast-failing with 400 and include `error_code: mixed_dims_in_batch` and `hint: use separate requests or use /batch-split header`. That allows SDK to auto-split.

emily: Exactly — SDK can split by dim automatically if we expose a clear contract or header. Right now it's guessing.

ops-bot: deploy 2024-06-14T15:22 succeeded to embeds-prod v2.7.3 (note for rollout).

ravi: Agree on two parts: runtime should detect mixed-dim early (preflight), and Console should surface telemetry for how many mixed-dim fast-fails happen, with sample requests. We should also avoid surfacing generic 413 for this class.

sara: UX question: what should Console show? A panel showing 'preflight rejections' with top reasons (mixed-dims, oversize-bytes, too-many-items) and example request sizes + tenant. Also a toggle to show opt-in auto-split suggestions.

tim: Implementation note: add a lightweight preflight (checksum + shape header) — e.g., clients send `X-Embed-Shape-Hint: dims=1024,1024,512;bytes=12345` and runtime does cheap validation and returns 200+warnings or 400+structured-error. No heavy deserialization.

emily: That header idea is good for back-compat. But we should also support server-side detection when header absent. The structured error must be stable: fields `error_code`, `reason`, `suggestion`, `split_plan` (split_plan could be an array of index ranges).

ravi: Concern: adding `split_plan` into errors may leak sensitive inputs. Let's limit sample to first token lengths and counts, not actual vectors. Also gate detailed samples behind internal console/telemetry only.

tim: For SDKs, return an error with `can_auto_split: true/false` and `suggested_batching` so SDK can retry automatically if tenant opts in. That avoids manual UX changes.

sara: From Console POV: telemetry should record error_code, tenant_id hash, request_size_bytes bucket, dims_signature (e.g., "1024x3,512x1"), and whether SDK auto-split succeeded. We can then surface a graph and an actionable 'enable auto-split for tenant' button for support.

emily: Quick repro note: I can make a minimal failing repro and file a bug. Would like to get a 2-week small project: preflight header + structured errors + console panel + SDK opt-in flow. Thoughts?

ravi: +1 but split into two sprints: (1) structured errors + runtime detection + minimal header; (2) Console telemetry + SDK auto-split + admin toggle.

tim: Dev details: runtime change needs to detect mismatched vector lengths in continuous batching path — cheap check on first input of each item. Risk: small perf hit if we check shapes per request. Proposal: check only when batch.IngestBarrier triggered or when bytes > threshold.

emily: OK let's start with a conservative preflight (header) and server detection on big batches. I'll draft the error schema: ```{
  "error_code": "mixed_dims_in_batch",
  "reason": "batch contains vectors with incompatible dimensionality",
  "suggestion": "split by dim or send via separate requests",
  "can_auto_split": "true",
  "split_plan": "[0-2]:1024, [3-3]:512"  // string to avoid nested JSON in top-level, SDK will parse
}```

sara: Please also include a short human message for Console and a machine message for SDKs. Console friendly: "Batch rejected: mixed vector dims — toggle to auto-split and retry."

ops-bot: alert: api-latency embeds-prod increased by 3% during canary 15:20-15:25.

ravi: Noted. Keep runtime cheap for first pass. Emily — can you own the RFC? I'll take runtime implementation and Tim will coordinate SDK changes. Sara, you'll own Console panel mockups.

emily: Yep. I'll open RFC + proto PR today with examples and repro. Will add sample SDK pseudocode for auto-split.

tim: One last ask — update client-side error handling docs to recommend header usage and show example of parsing `split_plan`.

emily: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
